subject: Privacy addendum follow-up: residency, subprocessors, and breach notification
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick privacy addendum follow-ups and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our call, wanted to summarize the three quick items your legal team asked us to clarify and propose next steps so we keep momentum for the pilot: 

1) Data residency: you indicated MedSync requires PHI to remain in the US-only environment for the pilot and any production integration. We can support US-only tenancy via Redwood Private (VPC) or by pinning to our US-hosted Dedicated pool.

2) Subprocessors: you asked for a current inventory and whether we provide subcontractor-level data access. We maintain a list of subprocessors and can provide a signed inventory; none have plaintext access to customer request payloads except for our managed infra provider for emergency support with logged access.

3) Breach notification timing and responsibilities: your counsel requested clarity on the timeframe we commit to for notifying customers and what evidence is included (logs, timeline). Our standard is to notify customers of confirmed breaches within 72 hours and share an incident timeline + relevant audit logs; we can commit to a 48-hour initial acknowledgement for high-severity incidents as an option in the addendum.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll circulate a redlined privacy addendum with the US-residency option and two notify-window choices (standard 72h, optional 48h acknowledgement). (Attachment: redwood_privacy_addendum_redline_v2.pdf)
- We’ll attach the current subprocessor inventory for your review (Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2028-05.csv).
- If helpful, legal can do a 30-minute sync with your counsel Thursday to walk through the redlines.

Can you confirm who from MedSync should receive the documents (legal + procurement email addresses)? Also, do you have an internal retention requirement for request/response logs (e.g., 12 months, 24 months)? We default to 13 months for request logs but can extend for enterprise contracts.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0191

---
Attachments: redwood_privacy_addendum_redline_v2.pdf (redline stub), subprocessor_inventory_2028-05.csv (list, stub)

Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 15:04:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick privacy addendum follow-ups and next steps

Jordan — great summary, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we loop in legal: 

- Residency: US-only is correct for the pilot. For production we may need EU-only or geo-fencing by customer in the future; please flag whether that’s a simple config or will require migration work.

- Subprocessors: please include whether any subprocessors are located outside the US and whether they have access to encryption keys or raw request payloads. Also note any SOC2 or ISO certifications.

- Breach timing: 72 hours is acceptable as a baseline. For healthcare customers we’d prefer the 48-hour acknowledgement option in the addendum. Also please confirm what we receive in the initial notification (we’ll need a classification of affected data types, whether PHI is involved, and the expected time to get a full timeline).

Procurement: procurement@medsynchealth.com is fine for docs; I’ll also add our GC if legal needs to do a call. Our request-log retention target is 24 months for the pilot cohort — can that be set as a contractual option?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Turner
Director, Digital Integrations | MedSync Health
Cell: +1 (206) 555-0122

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 17:23:15 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: quick privacy addendum follow-ups and next steps (legal draft)

Jordan / Ben — I reviewed Alex’s questions and put together suggested language and answers for each point. Quick notes below — I’ll attach the redline and subprocessor CSV to share with the customer once we agree.

1) Residency options: 
- US-only: checkbox on the addendum that pins to US-hosted Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC). Implementation note: Dedicated pin is instant; Private requires account provisioning (estimate: 3 business days).
- EU-only: possible but requires additional onboarding (data transfer controls and EU-hosted runtime). Flag to sales: ask if MedSync needs a hybrid model per customer.

2) Subprocessors and access: 
- Current inventory attached includes provider, location, access scope, and compliance certifications. None of our subprocessors have access to customer-managed encryption keys unless customer enables managed-key support; for customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) we note that subprocessors do not hold keys.
- Certifications: our infra provider holds SOC 2 Type II; we can provide attestation letters on request.

3) Breach notify / evidence package: 
- Default: notify of confirmed incidents within 72 hours with a classification and initial impact assessment.
- Enhanced: 48-hour initial acknowledgement for severity 1 incidents (non-investigative) included as an opt-in clause.
- Evidence: incident timeline, affected resource identifiers, redacted logs showing relevant request IDs, and remediation steps. Full forensic logs can be provided under an agreed request process.

4) Retention: 
- Default request/response logs retention: 13 months. Contractual options: 24 months (adds cost) or customer-managed export for long-term storage.

Action items: 
- Jordan: confirm we include the 48-hour opt-in clause and the 24-month retention option in the redline.
- Ben: please attach the subprocessor inventory CSV and confirm SOC2 attestation doc name.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the quick turn. We attached the two files you requested and provided the items Marissa called out. Summary below inline for your team and legal: 

- Residency: US-only is available as a contract checkbox. Production EU-only is possible; it’s a separate onboarding flow and we’ve called that out in the redline.

- Subprocessors: attached inventory lists location and access scope. Short answers: yes, some subprocessors operate outside the US (mainly support/monitoring providers in EMEA/APAC) but none have plaintext access to customer payloads unless emergency support is escalated and logged. Customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) prevents subprocessors from accessing plaintext or keys. SOC2 attestation is present for our infra provider; Ben attached the attestation filename in the CSV.

- Breach notify: we can offer the 48-hour initial acknowledgement opt-in and default 72-hour confirmed notification. Initial notification package will include: incident classification, whether PHI is affected, affected resource identifiers, and an estimated timeline for the full report. Full forensic logs available under a secure evidence request.

- Retention: we can offer 24 months as a contractual option for this pilot cohort; note it is billable.

Attached: redwood_privacy_addendum_redline_v2.pdf (redline with residency checkbox + notify options), subprocessor_inventory_2028-05.csv (includes attestation references).

If that addresses your asks, I’ll push the redline to procurement@medsynchealth.com and loop legal for a 30-minute call later this week. Proposed times: Thu 10:00 or Fri 09:00 PT.

Best — Jordan
